items.title: David Kelly of JPMorgan just told @CNBC that as long as wage gains are slow, the Fed shouldn't act to contain inflation. But inflation that excludes wages makes it an even bigger problem for workers, and therefore heightens the urgency for the Fed to do something to contain it.

items.title: The U.S. economy "unexpectedly" lost 23K jobs in July, while June's gain was revised down to a mere 20K. The unemployment rate slipped a bit because more people left the labor force, as the participation rate fell to 61.4%, the lowest in 50 years excluding COVID. Stagflation!

items.title: Copper is trading above $6.70 a pound, hitting a new all-time high. This does not bode well, given the Fed’s decisions not to raise interest rates and to open up the monetary spigots even more to keep Japan from selling Treasuries. Talk is cheap. The Fed can’t afford to act.
